key_insight: Thermodynamics-informed machine learning is needed to predict materials behavior realistically because free energies, not static lattice energies, control stability and functionality at finite temperature.
engineering_relevance: For energy materials design, ML models must capture entropy and anharmonic effects to reliably screen performance under operating conditions rather than only at 0 K.
method: Learn direct free-energy models instead of only static energies
Use machine-learned interatomic potentials and hybrid ML-statistical mechanics frameworks
Adopt entropy-aware representations and adaptive sampling across temperature
evidence_signal: The paper is a Perspective that synthesizes current approaches and challenges rather than reporting a new benchmark dataset or numerical evaluation.
watch_item: A key implementation risk is thermodynamic consistency and transferability, especially when training data are limited and temperature-dependent effects are underrepresented.
paper_title: Thermodynamics-Informed Machine Learning for Energy Materials Discovery
